source_read: PDF of the version of record, Drug Test Anal 2024;16(9):942–947, pp. 942–947 (all pages; Tables 1–2 checked on rendered pp. 944–945; supporting information not available)

claims.overstatement: The strip finding is accurate. The grouped attribution overstates this source: Sisco et al. (2024a) do not state that a positive result gives no amount. What they write is narrower: other α2-agonists would not be detected, so a negative could give 'a false sense of safety' (p. 946), and drug checking that identifies a range of substances is needed.
claims.note: Not supported for this source: 'and that a positive one gives no amount'. The α2-agonists in Table 1 that did not react at 100 µg/mL: clonidine, detomidine, medetomidine, romifidine, tizanidine (the table also lists etomidate, metamizole and tolazoline under that heading). Cross-reactivity was tested at one concentration only.

anchors.extracted: At 100 µg/mL only lidocaine read positive; no other compound reacted, including α2-agonists in the drug supply such as medetomidine (also clonidine, detomidine, romifidine, tizanidine); authors: these would not be detected, potentially creating a false sense of safety, so comprehensive drug checking is needed.
Other veterinary sedatives could go undetected with xylazine strips alone; consumers need services that identify a range of substances and inform them about drug contents.
Cross-reactivity was tested at 100 µg/mL only; the higher concentrations of dissolved powders could give different cross-reactivity.

claims.overstatement: The opening summary 'detected xylazine reliably when there was at least the strip's listed amount' goes beyond the pure-solution data: at the listed 1 µg/mL only 3 of 15 strips read positive, all 15 read positive only from 2.5 µg/mL, and the authors' own wording is consistent detection above 2 µg/mL (the one residue miss had 2 µg/mL). 'Reliably from about 2.5 times the listed amount; 37 of 38 residues at or above it read positive' would match. 'So these strips would not show them' holds at the 100 µg/mL tested; the authors say higher concentrations were not tested and could behave differently.
claims.note: Recomputed: 37/38 = 97.4% (Wilson 86.5–99.5%), 34/34 = 100% (89.8–100%), 43/66 = 65.2% (53.1–75.5%), all as in the claim; overall accuracy 71/72 = 98.6% as the paper says. '76 other compounds' matches Table 1 (77 entries including xylazine), whereas the abstract and §2.3 speak of a panel of 77. The residue cut-off is '>1 µg/ml' in the Methods text and '≥1' in Table 2 (printed as '³1'). In pure solution more strips read positive at 0.5 µg/mL (7/15) than at 1 µg/mL (3/15).

anchors.extracted: Xylazine ≥1 µg/mL by GC-MS/MS: 37 positive, 0 faint negative, 1 negative (n = 38); <1 µg/mL: 6, 10, 12 (n = 28; one sample with a negative and a faint negative counted negative); not detected: 0, 1, 33 (n = 34). Editors: sensitivity 97.4% (Wilson 86.5–99.5%), specificity 100% (89.8–100%), 43/66 xylazine-containing positive (65%; 53.1–75.5%).

66 of 100 residues held xylazine above the GC-MS/MS detection limit; the only miss above the cut-off was sample 63 (2 µg/mL); one faint negative among samples without xylazine; sensitivity 0.974, specificity 1.00, accuracy 0.986; results below 1 µg/mL inconsistent and left out of the calculation.

anchors.locator: Table 2, pure xylazine rows; §3.2 Limit of detection, 1st–2nd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: 15 strips per level over four days: 15/15 positive from 2.5 to 5000 µg/mL; 1 µg/mL 3 positive and 12 faint negative; 0.5 µg/mL 7 and 8; 0.1 and 0 µg/mL all negative. Limit (all replicates clearly positive) 2.5 µg/mL, slightly above the listed 1 µg/mL cut-off.

anchors.locator: §2 Materials and methods, 1st–2nd paragraphs; §2.4 Analysis of community-acquired samples, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: BTNX xylazine strips, listed cut-off 1 µg/mL; competitive assay: positive = no visible test band, faint negative recorded separately; 100 residue swabs from used syringes, plastic bags, wax bags and pill bottles in Maryland and Nevada, collected for another project; extracted in 1 mL acetonitrile, dried and taken up in 400 µL water for two strips per sample; GC-MS/MS on the same extract; DART-MS for identity.
Sensitivity and specificity computed only on samples above the 1 µg/mL cut-off (n = 38) and samples without xylazine (n = 34); the 28 below the cut-off presented without classification.

Panel described as 77 compounds (Table 1: 77 entries including xylazine) at 100 µg/mL, two strips each; only lidocaine positive (a prior study: lidocaine reacted at 10 but not 1 µg/mL); medetomidine, clonidine, detomidine, romifidine and tizanidine negative.
Residues rather than dissolved powders, whose higher concentrations could change cross-reactivity; all strips from a single production lot of a single maker.

key_findings.correction: Including the non-monotonic 7/15 at 0.5 against 3/15 at 1 µg/mL, also found in step 1.
My count of the rendered Table 1 is the same: 9 + 2 + 7 + 34 + 20 + 5 = 77 including xylazine.

Checked against Table S1 (project PDF Sisco_2024_XylazineTestStrips_SupplTable1.pdf): lidocaine in samples 42, 43, 6 and 12 (xylazine 74, 62, <0.5, <0.5 µg/mL); medetomidine in 67 and 94 (14, <0.5); all 34 xylazine-free samples N/N except sample 8 (FtN/FtN).

reporting_issues.note: Table S1 settles it: sample 40, at exactly 1 µg/mL, is classified TP and counted in the ≥1 group, so ≥ is the rule used and the text's '>' is the error.

Checked in the supplement docx and Table S1: the method text says values below 1 µg/mL were listed as <1, but Table S1 lists 0.5 (samples 35, 52, 55) and <0.5; DART-MS omits xylazine in samples 5 (55 µg/mL), 6, 12, 32 and 60.

risk_of_bias.note: Same as my own QUADAS-2 judgments: sample selection unclear, index test unclear, reference standard low, flow and timing high (28 of 100 samples left out of the headline accuracy), overall high.

missed: Table S1: the two residues holding lidocaine with xylazine below 0.5 µg/mL (samples 6 and 12) read faint negative on both strips, so lidocaine did not turn these residues positive (its amount is unknown, DART-MS being qualitative); key finding 11 could say so.
